newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken pressed to close Burundi brewery.
newsitem.headline: Heineken pressed to close Burundi brewery.

text.p: A delegation from the armed wing of Hutu-dominated Burundi opposition party Frodebu met with Dutch brewer Heineken on Monday, urging it to shut down its operations in the central African country, Heineken said.
"We had a frank exchange of views in a constructive atmosphere...but we said that the security of our personnel has to come first, " Heineken spokesman Koos Woltjes said.

Heineken said last Thursday it was stepping up beer production in the troubled African state after being told by the Burundi authorities that failure to do so would be construed as a political act against the Tutsi-led military government.
It said then that it feared failure to comply might endanger the safety of its employees.
Burundi's central African neighbours closed their borders against it following a Tutsi-led military coup in July.

"The delegation from (Frodebu armed wing) CNGD acknowledged we had not breached the embargo, and expressed understanding of our concern for the safety of our employees, but said we had to deal with the higher political goal," Woltjes said.
"However one cannot ask a company...to tell its personnel that their safety is secondary," he added.
Heineken owns a 60 percent stake in local brewer Barudi, which has two plants and a total production capacity of 1.2 million hectolitres.
The Burundi government, which owns a 40 percent Barudi stake, had imported malt from neighbouring Rwanda and told Heineken it expected production to be increased, Woltjes said.
Before last week's decision the brewer had been operating at 25 percent capacity, he said.

He said the level of production in future would depend on demand, adding that widespread breaches of the embargo by neighbouring African states meant demand would likely increase. (( -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040))
